doc.title: Frank Capp interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Boston University and percussion training
summary: Capp left Boston University in his junior year to join Kenton, never finishing his degree; his classical percussion training served him later in the studios.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: You must have had some, from the work you’re describing, did you have some actual percussion training when you were young or has it kind of been —

You know oddly enough, I can still hear my mother reprimanding me for not practicing. Can’t hear him practice. And I did have some training. I went to Boston University and I was in Boston University when Stan called me to join the band. So I left I think in my junior year. I never got my degree. But I had enough classical training as a percussionist to get me through most of what I would need later in the studios. Because as a nineteen year old, my aspirations were to be a big band jazz drummer. And I’ve never lost that aspiration. I’m still trying to be a big band jazz drummer.
That must be a great feeling — to drive a big band — I would think.

Yeah. I enjoy it very much. I love working with my band, but I love working with a lot of other bands, as you just mentioned, this weekend is pretty busy with me. And tomorrow I’m going to be down at the Marriott where there’s another jazz party going on with Terry Gibbs Dream Band.
